title: piv: PKCS#11 slot enumeration and challenge signing
description:
hire-attestors/src/piv.rs is the emptiest module that still claims to exist. is_available() returns FALSE IN BOTH cfg ARMS (:25-31) -- the pkcs11 arm hardcodes false behind a ponytail comment naming cryptoki as the upgrade -- so the source never activates even when built with --features pkcs11. The pkcs11 feature itself is an empty placeholder with no dependency (hire-attestors/Cargo.toml). And prove() is the default refusal.

Real work, in order: add cryptoki, enumerate slots, find the PIV application, read the certificate, sign the challenge with the card's key.

WHY IT MATTERS DISPROPORTIONATELY: this is the CAC path. SPEC-HIRE notes the certificate may carry UPN, email, or DOD EDIPI, and the whole 2028 high-security scenario on persona-3tly assumes card-based identity is real here. It is also the source persona-3tly.6 names as having genuine DEPARTURE detection -- a PC/SC card-removal event is an observed fact, not a timeout -- which makes it the natural first implementation of the departure half of the presence model.

Presence depends on PIN mode, which makes it a prompting attestor: same persona-jl4j.3 constraint as fido2.

Assurance iaa3 when the card is hardware-bound and a PIN is required.
acceptance_criteria: A signature from the card over the daemon's challenge; is_available() reflects an actual slot probe rather than a constant; PIN-mode determines the presence claim; proof cost declared.
